newsitem.title: CROATIA: Opposition slams Tudjman, police ahead of polls.
newsitem.headline: Opposition slams Tudjman, police ahead of polls.

text.p: Croatian opposition parties on Monday criticised President Franjo Tudjman for using his official position to campaign for Sunday's presidential election.

They also said they were unhappy with the way the authorities had handled an incident in which his rival Vlado Gotovac, supported by nine parties, was struck on the head by a Croatian army soldier at a rally on Thursday.

"President Tudjman is using not only his regular presidential activities but also a vast amount of Croatian tax-payers' money for his self-promotion," Stjepo Martinovic of the Croatian People's party told a joint oposition news conference.

The 75-year old Tudjman rode on a "train of freedom" to the last Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia on Sunday to call for reconciliation between Serbs and Croats. The enclave, administered by the United Nations, is due to revert to Croatian rule in mid-July.
"What has changed in Vukovar (the enclave's capital) after his visit? Nothing. It was a vain parade to satisfy an old dictator," Martinovic said.

Gotovac, leader of the Social Liberal party (HSLS), was released from hospital and was feeling better after suffering concussion, but was advised by doctors to curtail his campaign to avoid travelling, HSLS secretary Karl Gorinsek said.
The 66-year-old Gotovac was struck with a heavy belt buckle by a man wearing army uniform at a rally in the Adriatic town of Pula.
"The (attack) is a serious setback for the HSLS and all opposition parties. I hope it will not affect the will of voters," Gorinsek said.

The attacker was later identified as Croatian army captain Tomislav Brzovic who, according to the HSLS, was a member of Tudjman's security guard. The Defence Ministry said Brzovic had been immediately suspended from duty and detained.
But Gorinsek said that was not nearly enough.

"There were failures on the part of civilian and military police before and during the rally. They were not energetic enough with Brzovic," Gorinsek said, adding the party had heard of other violent incidents he had been involved in.

"We are not satisfied because we haven't had a report on the progress of the investigation from the interior or defence ministry. The public has to know what concrete steps are being taken against the perpetrator," Gorinsek said.

Tudjman is widely expected to brush aside Gotovac and another candidate, Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democrats, and win a clear victory in the first round of voting on the strength of his popular reputation as the man who created independent Croatia.
